questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Mrs. Lisa suggested that we should purchase the property.

options.text: Mrs. Lisa said, "Property must be purchased by us."
Mrs. Lisa said, "Please purchase the property."
Mrs. Lisa said, "Let us purchase the property."
Mrs. Lisa told, "You may purchase the property."

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **3) Mrs. Lisa said, "Let us purchase the property."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "Let's purchase the property" is grammatically the most accurate representation of “suggested that we should”.
 
• The phrase **“Let us...”** is commonly used to express suggestions involving both the speaker and listener.
 
• It retains both the first-person plural (we) and the suggestive tone, making it an accurate conversion into direct speech.

Hence, the correct answer is: ***Mrs. Lisa said, "Let us purchase the property."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's see why the other options are incorrect.

 
• **Option 1: Mrs. Lisa said, "Property must be purchased by us."**

 
 
• This is a passive construction using "must," which indicates compulsion, not suggestion.
 
• The tone here is stronger and forceful, and does not reflect the suggestion implied in the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Mrs. Lisa said, "Please purchase the property."**
 
 
• This is a polite request, using "please."
 
• It directs the action to someone else (you) and does not include Mrs. Lisa in the action.
 
• The original sentence has "we," indicating that Mrs. Lisa is part of the group doing the purchasing, so this changes the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Mrs. Lisa told, "You may purchase the property."**
 
 
• This uses “told” without an object (incorrect grammar – "told" requires an object, e.g., "told us"),
 
• It also changes the subject to “you” and implies permission, not suggestion, and excludes the speaker from the action.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. He exclaimed that he was a very stupid fellow.

options.text: "How a stupid fellow are you!" he remarked.
"How a stupid fellow you are!" he remarked.
"Are you a stupid fellow!" he remarked.
"What a stupid fellow you are!" he remarked.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He exclaimed that he was a very stupid fellow.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"he was a very stupid fellow" becomes "What a stupid fellow you are"**
 
 
• The exclamatory sentence structure is retained by changing the pronoun "he" to "you".
 
• The adjective "stupid" remains the same, and the sentence is structured to reflect direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "exclaimed"
 
• Converted to: "remarked", suitable for direct speech expression.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "What" and ends with an exclamation mark "!".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“What a stupid fellow you are!” he remarked."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "How a stupid fellow are you!" he remarked. 
 
 
• Incorrect sentence structure for an exclamatory sentence in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "How a stupid fellow you are!" he remarked. 
 
 
• Although close, the phrase "How a stupid fellow" is not idiomatic in English.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Are you a stupid fellow!" he remarked. 
 
 
• Changes the exclamatory sentence into a question, altering the meaning.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said, "Bravo! You have done well."

options.text: She told her saying that she had done well.
She applauded her saying that she had done well.
She applauded her saying that she did well.
She applauded her saying that she has done well.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She applauded her saying that she had done well.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Bravo! You have done well." becomes "She applauded her saying that she had done well."**
 
 
• Exclamatory sentence "Bravo!" is converted to the verb "applauded."
 
• Direct speech "You have done well" is changed to indirect speech "she had done well."
 
 
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:** 
 
 
• Direct: "said"
 
• Converted to: "applauded," indicating praise.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She applauded her saying that she had done well."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She told her saying that she had done well." 

 
 
• Does not convey the exclamatory praise "Bravo!"
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She applauded her saying that she did well."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "did" instead of "had done."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She applauded her saying that she has done well." 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "has done" instead of "had done."
